summary: No region-specific signal on transgender travel safety was identified for the Cordillera Administrative Region; the national assessment for the Philippines applies, and the full national layer is carried by the parent record.
tangentialFactors: Justice in Kalinga operates in part through the bodong/pagta customary system, in which bodong holders resolve criminal and tribal offences alongside the formal courts, with Philippine National Police personnel, prosecutors and barangay officials taking part in customary conflict resolution. The sources do not record how that system handles complaints involving sexual orientation or gender identity, so its effect on a trans complainant in the province is unresolved.
localsOnly: For residents, the inventory records no region-specific anti-discrimination ordinance or protection on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity across Abra, Apayao, Benguet, Ifugao, Kalinga, Mountain Province or Baguio; residents depend on the national patchwork of sectoral statutes and on ordinances adopted in other parts of the country.
outOfScopeNotes: One source in the inventory concerns the Central African Republic rather than the Cordillera Administrative Region, and no claim from it is used here. The inventory contains no documentation of enforcement practice, incidents, or detention and facilities policy specific to the region, so no regional finding on those points can be made.
